platform: stock CheriBSD purecap built on this host (kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, releng/26.07-88f39900c329 = pins.env CHERIBSD_REV)

prediction.why: the crossing leaves the alpha PLANE but stays inside the frame's single AVBuffer -- measured slack 1024 bytes against a logical 160 -- and CHERI bounds the allocation, not the plane. A FAULT here would have meant the reduction is not doing what it claims, not that CHERI improved.

what_this_closes: the LAST unmeasured cheribsd-revocation arm of the 54 cases across the paper's three programs; the other 53 were already measured. The three-program CheriBSD column is now 54/54 measured.
why_it_was_unrun: this corpus links REAL libavutil (av_frame_get_buffer carves the planes), unlike its plain-heap siblings which link nothing, so a purecap libavutil had to exist first. One was cross-built out of tree with the CHERI SDK and verified by ELF flags (EF_RISCV_CAP_MODE, EF_RISCV_CHERIABI, EM_RISCV) rather than by the build command's intent.
instrument_fixes_required_first: the read probe was __attribute__((noinline, used)) static in shared/corpus.h, so supervise could never resolve it by name and every arm would have read UNRESOLVED; it is now ffp_read_probe, defined once in shared/driver.c (nm: T ffp_read_probe)

the runner's purecap guard originally piped llvm-readobj into `grep -q`, which closes the pipe at the first match so readobj dies of SIGPIPE and, under `set -o pipefail`, the pipeline reports non-zero -- the guard rejected a library that IS purecap. The check now captures the output instead of piping into a gate.
guard_negative_tested: pointing FFPURECAP at the NATIVE libavutil.a gives exit 75 and 'is not a purecap archive', so the purecap guard is proven two-sided rather than merely passing
